name: Zapotec, Mitla
catalog_quote: Stress in Mitla Zapoteco is non-phonemic; stress occurs on stem-final syllables in all words studied. ... word-final juncture, stress and laryngealization are absent, except when word-final juncture coincides with stem-final juncture.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: no Briggs 1961 file is held; the deciding Briggs pp.7-8 wording is snippet-grade and could not be re-verified today (Google Books captcha, archive.org offline). (2) But the held Stubblefield & Hollenbach 1991 SIL grammar sketch, read from page images, states the same system at page grade: word accent falls on the final ROOT; complex vowels survive only under stress; 3sg -ni, 1pl -nu and the enclitic adverbs are unstressed; root-like 'dependent adverbs' (-ro, -gajc, -duxh...) take the stress as last root of a compound. This matches the record's domain statement (stem-final, word-final only when the word ends in its stem; compounds stressed on the last stem) and the morph-split/dominant-final handling. One refinement not in the record: 1sg -ä takes the word stress after a broken or aspirated root vowel (baslaä 'solté') but not after a checked vowel (§0.3) — a suffix-specif

sources.quote: p. 7: "Stress in Mitla Zapoteco is non-phonemic; stress occurs on stem-final syllables in all words studied. The placement of stress in Mitla Zapoteco seems contrary to that of other Zapoteco languages, which may have stress occurring on other syllables than the stem-final one." Corroborating p. 3: "... a lowered allotone in final un-stressed syllable: ge?-ni 'it is lime', bya?N-lu 'you stayed', ba.wi 'look', gu.läb-ni 'it boiled'."
sources.note: It is the deciding source of record and we hold it only as Google Books scanned snippets; page images of pp. 3, 7, 8 would lift the deciding quote to page grade, settle the ba.wi 'look' parse flagged in the owner note, and show whether the stem-final rule carries any loanword qualification.

sources.quote: §0.2: 'El acento prosódico de la palabra cae sobre la raíz final, y las vocales complejas (las no sencillas) se presentan solamente en las sílabas acentuadas. Así que, las vocales complejas se cambian por las vocales sencillas correspondientes cuando se presentan en las sílabas no finales de las palabras compuestas ... -ro grande y -gajc luego son raíces, y producen un cambio de la vocal, mientras que el pronombre inseparable -ni tercera persona no provoca ningún cambio.' (bisíáa+-ró -> bisiaró; bisíáa+-ni -> bisiáani; dá'+-ró -> daró; dá'+-ni -> dá'ni; basláa+-gájc+-ni -> baslagájcni). §0.3:
